draft.title: Congruent figures
card: Congruent figures are exactly the same shape and the same size. One would fit exactly on top of the other.
Matching sides are equal in length and matching angles are equal in size. Matching parts are in the same position in each figure.
A figure can be turned or flipped and still be congruent. Moving it does not change its shape or size.
Example: triangle \(ABC\) is congruent to triangle \(PQR\), and side \(AB\) is 5 cm. Then the matching side \(PQ\) is also 5 cm. If angle \(C\) is \(40^{\circ}\), angle \(R\) is \(40^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: Congruent means identical in shape and size, so matching parts are equal, even after a turn or flip.

a.q: Quadrilateral \(EFGH\) is congruent to quadrilateral \(WXYZ\), with \(E\) matching \(W\) and \(F\) matching \(X\). Side \(EF\) is 8 cm. What is the length of \(WX\)?
a.why: \(WX\) matches \(EF\), and matching sides of congruent figures are equal. So \(WX\) is 8 cm. It is not 4 cm or 16 cm, because congruent figures are the same size, so no length is halved or doubled.
a.clue: Matching sides of congruent figures are equal.

b.q: Mia cuts a paper triangle, flips it over and traces around it. Which statement about the two triangles is true?
opts: They are congruent, as flipping keeps shape and size
They are not congruent, as a flip changes the shape
They are not congruent, as the angles are reversed
They are congruent only if she turns it instead of flipping
b.why: A flip moves a figure but does not change its shape or size, so the triangles are congruent. The tempting idea is that a flipped figure looks different. Looking different in position does not matter, because matching sides and angles are still equal.
b.clue: Does flipping change any side length or angle size?

b.best: They are congruent, as flipping keeps shape and size
